subject: Travel arrangements for next week
text: Good morning, please see the current travel plan for the team. The client requires confirmation by noon on Thursday, and we cannot delay the booking once approvals are closed. The outbound flight departs from Terminal 2. The arrival is after dinner, so transport should be arranged in advance. Please check the attached summary for names, dates, and budget lines. If any traveler has an accessibility need, let me know as soon as possible. The hotel room block is tentative until the final list is approved. The train option remains available, but it will require a later arrival and a separate receipt. Please choose one option for each traveler. Do not reply with more than one option per person. If a colleague must switch seats, note the original selection in the subject line of their reply. For the meeting, the room is held for six people. The address has been shared through the calendar invitation, not in this message. Please confirm attendance by email. The deadline is firm because the vendor closes access to the venue at the end of the day. If you cannot meet it, please send a short note with the reason and the alternative contact who can decide. I will compile the final details after the group responds. If there is a conflict, I will try to adjust one item, not the whole schedule. This keeps the costs stable and avoids duplicate bookings. Please do not forward this message outside the group without warning, as the room allocation is not yet final. Your prompt reply will help us complete the arrangements quietly and on time.
